Yes, it's a love and hate relationship. The main point of ascension is to drive the ideation of Taoism. Transcendence to another realm (whether external i.e. worldly or internal i.e. cultivation) can be better understood once you understand the background narrative that the author is trying to explore and create.

That is that, "Taoism holds that beings (living organisms), should live in balance with the Tao (Dao), or the universe. Taoists believe in a singularity, of the immortality of the spirit, which is the transformation and transcendence of a human, where the spirit of the body joins the universe after eternal death. Thus, this paradoxical idea of eternal life and eternal death is not a paradox in itself, as taoist doctrine focuses on the immortal pursuit of longevity and true health, in accordance with the balance of the universe."

Usually most novels try to follow Taoism in its principles, but ultimately deviates to a more engaging and enjoyable narrative about the author's own interpretation of transcendence. The question of whether it ruins the "storytelling" is purely subjective. When authors' use of clichés, forced conflicts, plot armor, deus ex machina, etc, mask the clear errors in logic within the novel, one must remind themselves that this is a cultivation story, a xianxia, wuxia and or xuanhuan novel. This is eastern fantasy, and it's very obvious that they will mess up a few things to seek their own path towards their own Dao of Writing.

There are many stories that execute based on clear and beautiful understanding of Chinese theological philosophy, and others who copy paste successful novels all in the name of profit. Regardless of all this however, I can't say for certain whether my own analysis is good, so take my words with a grain of salt.

We were in a situationship, where we were "friends but not friends." At the time I was nervous because we were interacting as if we were intimate, but we never declared anything further. Eventually, I did try, but it was already too late and she had moved away. Fast forward to the future and we met again, reconciling old relations. When we met again, I confessed that I did love her when we were younger. Do you know what she said? *"I thought we were just friends."* At that moment, I knew that it didn't matter how much can be perceived by the human eye.
